description: Final-year Computer Science student at Tshwane University of Technology. I build browser apps in TypeScript, React, and Next.js. We are making a no-login game for ages 7-12: a lunar south-pole outpost where every choice spends power, air, or shielding, using real NASA data. Looking for a writer, a designer, and someone to record a 2-minute demo.
summary:
AstraOrbit In-Suit OS is a medical support app built for astronauts on deep space missions. When Earth is far away and communication is delayed, crews still need clear health guidance. That is what AstraOrbit provides through Dr. Astra, an on-suit clinical assistant that explains what is happening and what to do next in plain language.

The system brings together health readiness scores, medication tracking with dosing guidance, a clickable 2D/3D body map, behavioral and imaging tools, and accessibility support for parastronauts. It also pulls live NASA DONKI space weather data so radiation and spacewalk advice can change with real solar flares, particle storms, CMEs, and geomagnetic conditions.

This matters because NASA’s Human Research Program points to five core spaceflight hazards: delayed care from Earth, radiation, isolation, distance, and limited resources. AstraOrbit keeps clinical decision support with the crew, so they can act sooner, stay safer, and rely less on constant Mission Control contact during Mars class missions.
details:
AstraOrbit is an insuit clinical decision support system and electronic health record for deep space crews. Astronauts open a single interface to check readiness, review vitals, manage medications, inspect body regions on a 2D or 3D map, log behavioral status, and ask Dr. Astra for plain english guidance when Earth contact is delayed. Live NASA DONKI space weather data updates radiation and EVA risk (green / yellow / red), so advice follows real solar conditions instead of fixed assumptions.

How it works: Crew health inputs and mission context feed a readiness score and alert layer. Dr. Astra uses offline edge logic first, with optional cloud AI when available, and always stays within clinical and NASA HRP “five hazards” scope. Space weather sync runs behind the scenes from a secured NASA API key; astronauts only see weather status and can ask Dr. Astra if they need help interpreting it.

Benefits & impact: Faster, clearer decisions during communication lag; radiation aware EVA caution; medication dosing support; inclusive design for parastronauts; and less dependence on continuous Mission Control for routine clinical questions. The intended impact is safer crew autonomy on mars class missions.

Tools & stack: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, SCSS, Three.js (3D body map), Web Speech API (voice), NASA DONKI API, optional Gemini for CDSS replies, plus Python tools for presentation/demo media. Deployed as a static web app (Porkbun Secure Static Hosting) for easy sharing.

Creative approach: We treated the spacesuit as a clinical workstation weather, body map, meds, and AI in one flow using plain language instead of dense medical jargon, and designing for accessibility from the start.

Team considerations: Delayed communications, radiation risk, resource limits, clinical safety wording, inclusive access, and a public demo that judges can open without installing software.
